response: Based on your project's current state at 5 months of development with working CRUD operations, I've created a strategic roadmap focusing on the critical next phase: improving LLM reliability, implementing RAG systems, and building the core intelligent features that differentiate your product. These initiatives are ordered to build foundational capabilities first, then layer on the intelligent features that will deliver value to your target users.
title: Strategic Roadmap: From Polish to Intelligent Product Management
reasoning: The project is past basic CRUD and entering the polish/intelligence phase. The main pain points are LLM reliability and RAG implementation. Initiatives prioritize solving these foundational issues before building higher-level features like cross-team consistency detection and agentic coding integration.

initiatives.name: LLM Reliability & Prompt Engineering Framework
initiatives.description: Establish a robust framework for managing LLM interactions with consistent, reliable outputs across all product features
initiatives.details: Build a centralized prompt management system with versioning, A/B testing capabilities, and output validation. Implement structured output parsing with fallback strategies, retry logic with exponential backoff, and comprehensive logging for debugging. Create prompt templates for each use case (initiative generation, design document creation, work item breakdown, consistency checking) with clear instructions and examples. Include temperature and token limit configurations per use case. Implement output validation schemas using tools like Pydantic or JSON Schema to ensure LLM responses match expected formats. Build monitoring dashboards to track success rates, latency, and token usage per prompt type.
initiatives.acceptanceCriteria:
- Centralized prompt management system with version control implemented
- Structured output validation with >90% parse success rate
- Retry logic and fallback strategies reduce failure rate to <5%
- Monitoring dashboard tracks key metrics (success rate, latency, cost) per prompt type
- Documentation covers prompt engineering best practices and troubleshooting
- A/B testing framework allows comparing prompt variations
initiatives.reasoning: This addresses the stated 'considerable amount of pain dealing with getting reliable results from llms' and is foundational for all AI-powered features. Without reliable LLM outputs, higher-level features will be unreliable.

influences.reasoning: User explicitly mentioned 'considerable amount of pain dealing with getting reliable results from llms' as a current challenge
Multiple AI-powered features described require reliable LLM outputs

initiatives.name: RAG System Implementation for Project Context
initiatives.description: Build and deploy RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) systems to provide contextual information retrieval across initiatives, designs, code, and conversations
initiatives.details: Implement a multi-tenant vector database (e.g., Pinecone, Weaviate, or Qdrant) to store embeddings of project artifacts including initiatives, design documents, ADRs, code snippets, PR descriptions, and chat history. Create chunking strategies optimized for different content types (code vs prose). Build indexing pipelines that automatically embed new content as it's created or updated. Implement hybrid search combining vector similarity with keyword matching for better precision. Create retrieval strategies for different use cases: (1) answering user questions about the project, (2) providing context to agents for longer-running tasks, (3) detecting design inconsistencies. Include relevance scoring and re-ranking to surface the most pertinent information. Build APIs that allow external tools (via MCP) to query project context.
initiatives.acceptanceCriteria:
- Vector database deployed with multi-tenant isolation
- Automatic indexing pipeline processes all project artifacts (initiatives, designs, code, conversations)
- Retrieval API returns relevant context with <500ms p95 latency
- Hybrid search demonstrates >80% relevance in user testing
- MCP server exposes project context to external tools
- Documentation covers chunking strategies and retrieval optimization
initiatives.reasoning: User stated 'We need to get our RAG systems up and running' as a critical next step. This enables the core value proposition of providing full project context to AI and team members, and is required for the agent system.

initiatives.name: Agent Framework for Long-Running Tasks
initiatives.description: Develop an agent system that can execute multi-step tasks by pulling information from multiple sources and maintaining context over extended periods
initiatives.details: Build an agent orchestration framework that can plan, execute, and monitor long-running tasks. Implement a task queue system (e.g., Celery, BullMQ) for async execution. Create agent capabilities including: (1) querying RAG system for project context, (2) making API calls to external services (GitHub, etc.), (3) generating and validating design documents, (4) breaking down initiatives into work items, (5) detecting design inconsistencies. Implement a state machine to track agent progress through multi-step workflows with checkpointing for recovery. Build a feedback loop where agents can ask clarifying questions to users when needed. Include monitoring and observability to track agent actions, decisions, and outcomes. Create safeguards to prevent runaway execution (token limits, step limits, human-in-the-loop checkpoints).
initiatives.acceptanceCriteria:
- Agent framework can execute multi-step workflows with state persistence
- Agents successfully query RAG system for contextual information
- Task queue handles async execution with retry logic
- Agents can generate design documents and break them into work items
- Monitoring dashboard shows agent execution traces and outcomes
- Human-in-the-loop checkpoints prevent unintended actions
- At least 3 agent workflows implemented (e.g., initiative breakdown, design validation, consistency checking)
initiatives.reasoning: Agents are central to the product vision for automating tedious work and are explicitly mentioned as needed for longer-running tasks. This builds on the RAG foundation to deliver intelligent automation.

initiatives.name: GitHub Integration & Code Validation Pipeline
initiatives.description: Build bidirectional GitHub integration to push work items and pull completed code for validation against design specifications
initiatives.details: Implement GitHub OAuth authentication and repository connection. Create workflows to: (1) export work items as GitHub issues with full context, (2) monitor PR creation and updates via webhooks, (3) automatically pull PR content and diffs into the system when work is marked complete. Build a validation pipeline that uses RAG to retrieve original design specs and initiative context, then uses LLMs to analyze code changes against requirements. Generate validation reports highlighting: alignment with design, potential inconsistencies with other work, code quality concerns, missing requirements. Provide a UI for reviewing validation results with links to specific code sections and design documents. Support commenting back to GitHub PRs with validation feedback. Include configuration for which repositories and branches to monitor.
initiatives.acceptanceCriteria:
- OAuth flow connects user GitHub accounts and repositories
- Work items can be exported as GitHub issues with full context
- Webhook integration detects PR creation and updates in real-time
- Validation pipeline analyzes code changes against design specifications
- Validation reports identify alignment issues with >70% accuracy in testing
- UI displays validation results with actionable feedback
- System can comment on GitHub PRs with validation insights
- Configuration allows selecting specific repos and branches to monitor
initiatives.reasoning: GitHub integration is explicitly mentioned in the core workflow and is essential for the end-to-end experience from planning to validation. This closes the loop on the development workflow.

initiatives.name: Design Consistency Detection & Alert System
initiatives.description: Implement intelligent monitoring to detect design inconsistencies and incompatibilities across concurrent initiatives before they become integration problems
initiatives.details: Build a background monitoring system that periodically analyzes all active initiatives, design documents, and work items to detect potential conflicts. Use RAG to gather context about related work across teams. Implement detection algorithms for: (1) naming inconsistencies (e.g., different casing for same entities), (2) API contract mismatches between producer and consumer, (3) conflicting architectural decisions, (4) duplicate or overlapping work, (5) dependency conflicts. Use LLMs to analyze retrieved context and identify subtle inconsistencies that rule-based systems would miss. Generate alerts with severity levels (critical, warning, info) and actionable recommendations. Create a dashboard showing detected issues with links to affected artifacts. Allow users to dismiss false positives or acknowledge and track resolution. Implement notification system (in-app, email) for critical issues.
initiatives.acceptanceCriteria:
- Background job runs consistency checks on configurable schedule
- System detects naming inconsistencies across initiatives with >80% accuracy
- API contract mismatches are identified between related work items
- Alerts include severity levels and actionable recommendations
- Dashboard displays all detected issues with filtering and sorting
- Users can dismiss false positives and track issue resolution
- Notification system alerts relevant team members of critical issues
- Detection algorithms cover at least 5 categories of inconsistencies
initiatives.reasoning: This is a key differentiator mentioned in the core goals: 'detect design discrepancies ahead of time we can save significant engineering waste.' It builds on RAG and agent capabilities to deliver proactive value.

influences.reasoning: Core goal explicitly mentions 'detect design discrepancies ahead of time we can save significant engineering waste'

initiatives.name: MCP Server for Agentic Coding Tool Integration

initiatives.details: Build an MCP-compliant server that exposes project information and capabilities as tools/resources that external AI coding assistants can query. Implement MCP resources for: (1) retrieving initiative details, (2) fetching design documents and ADRs, (3) searching project context via RAG, (4) getting work item specifications, (5) querying validation results. Implement MCP tools for: (1) creating work items, (2) updating task status, (3) requesting design clarifications. Include authentication and authorization to ensure secure access. Build rate limiting and usage monitoring to prevent abuse. Create documentation and examples showing how to connect Claude Code and other MCP-compatible tools. Test integration with Claude Code to validate the end-to-end experience described in the vision.
